verdict: THE QUESTION WAS WRONG, NOT THE DATA. Four modules concluded that a Reactome reaction cannot orient a PPI edge, because only 95 of 36,415 co-participating edges split across input and output while 1,593 sit on the same side. The error was treating the huge 'appears on both sides' bucket as ambiguity. Reactome mints a NEW entity id for every modified form, so in a phosphorylation the SUBSTRATE appears on both sides as two different entities while the KINASE appears as the same entity twice. Comparing leaf-entity sets per gene therefore separates the acted-upon (transformed) from the actor (unchanged), and the arrow is unchanged -> transformed. MEASURED: 3,822 PPI edges oriented (2.00% of the interactome), accuracy 0.8326 +/- 0.0146 on n=657, against a MATCHED degree baseline of 0.5373 on the same edges -- a gain of +0.2953, which is far too large to be the degree rule in disguise. The cluster bootstrap over 710 reactions, which is the correct interval because one reaction emits many arrows that are right or wrong together, gives [0.8111, 0.8661]. Splitting by what changed: chemical modification 0.8495 (n=618) versus translocation 0.6860 (n=86) -- reported separately, because folding them together would let the higher number be quoted over edges that do not earn it. A CORRECTION THIS FORCES: earlier modules called 0.783 a 'curated-vs-curated ceiling'. This exceeds it. That figure was the agreement rate between two specific curated sources over the edges they share, where disagreement is dominated by TF pairs whose two arrows are both true. It was never a bound on accuracy, and describing it as a ceiling is withdrawn. WHAT IT STILL CANNOT SAY: Reactome describes canonical human biology, not K562; Reactome and SIGNOR curators read overlapping literature, so this is not fully independent validation; and coverage remains the binding constraint -- only 3,164 PPI edges (1.65%) have any unambiguous curated direction at all, so every accuracy here describes that slice, not the network.
